# ethereum-optimism/design-docs Weekly Report (Apr 19 - 25, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week focused on refining protocol specifications for the upcoming Osaka upgrade and resolving critical stability issues within the interoperability and testing frameworks. Significant progress was made in stabilizing the CI/CD pipeline by addressing multiple flaky tests, including a major resolution for `TestFlashblocksTransfer`. Developers also finalized several interoperability enhancements for Kona and clarified the transition timeline for execution clients, confirming support for `op-geth` through late May.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Protocol Specifications & Documentation
The team continued to iterate on the design documents for the Osaka upgrade on L2.
*   **Osaka Upgrade Refinement:** Documentation was updated to standardize naming conventions, transitioning from "fusaka" to "osaka" in the protocol specs ([#376](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/376)). A new PR was also opened to specifically address FMA (Fast Message Authenticity) for Osaka ([#375](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/375)).
*   **Template Improvements:** The design document template now includes a mandatory reminder regarding the use of third-party services to ensure better compliance and architectural oversight ([#373](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/373)).
*   **SDM Integration:** Work is underway to move Superchain Dependency Manager (SDM) PoC2 functionality into the `develop` branch and integrate SDM specs into the official documentation ([#20182](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/20182), [#20216](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/20216)).

### Infrastructure & CI/CD
*   **CircleCI for Forks:** A new initiative was launched to enable CircleCI for pull requests originating from forks, which will significantly improve the contribution experience for external developers ([#377](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/377)).
*   **Protocol Cleanup:** The legacy request-response P2P sync mechanism in `op-node` was officially deprecated and closed in favor of more modern unsafe block sync protocols ([#14108](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/14108)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **Interoperability & Kona:** Several issues regarding `kona-node` were resolved, including a fix for output root mismatches during message expiry consolidation and the conditional deployment of `CrossL2Inbox` ([#19848](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19848), [#19311](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19311)).
*   **Contract Feature Flags:** Implementation of the `OPSuccinct` feature flag within the Optimism Portal and Contract Manager (OPCM) was completed ([#18419](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/18419), [#18420](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/18420)).
*   **Batcher Throttling:** Confirmed that `op-reth` and `op-rbuilder` already support necessary batcher throttling, allowing these issues to be closed ([#18764](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/18764)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **Flaky Test Investigation:** This week saw a concerted effort to fix race conditions in the test suite. While `TestFlashblocksTransfer` is now "probably fixed" after 37 consecutive passes ([#19934](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19934)), new investigations were opened for `TestSequencingWindowExpiry` (race condition in `OpProofsExEx`) and `TestUnsafeGapFillAfterUnsafeReorg` ([#20212](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/20212), [#19936](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19936)).
*   **Kona Block Access:** Ongoing discussions involve how `kona-proofs` handles internally created blocks. A potential bug was identified where receipts for replaced deposit-only blocks are not stored, which could cause failures during message graph resolution ([#19266](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19266)).
*   **Sequencer Engine Resets:** A new issue tracks a bug where `op-node` in "sequencer LightCL" mode performs unnecessary engine resets on restart, potentially rewinding execution layer heads ([#20294](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/20294)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The community sought clarification on the transition from `op-geth` to `op-reth`. Maintainers clarified that `op-geth` remains supported until May 31st, while acknowledging a current gap in documentation and support for `op-reth` within the `simple-optimism-node` setup ([#20203](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/20203)). Additionally, users reported build failures for finalized Docker image tags for `op-node` and `kona-node`, with the team providing temporary workarounds using `-rc.1` images while the release pipeline is fixed ([#20228](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/20228)).
